newsitem.title: USA: TransTexas drills 'major' Bob West stepout.
newsitem.headline: TransTexas drills 'major' Bob West stepout.

text.p: TransTexas Gas Corp said Tuesday it had drilled and logged a well to the far north of its Bob West North natural gas field that represented a major stepout and extension of the field.

The R. Santos 1 was drilled 3.2 miles north-northwest of previous Bob West North field production and exposes a new fault block of the structure that had previously not been drilled, the company said.
It said electric logs of the well indicated as much as 200 feet of pay in the Roletta and Upper Wilcox formations.

TransTexas said that the addition of this new fault block has the potential to double natural gas reserves recoverable from the field since it confirms the presence of gas bearing sands all the way to the Rio Grande.

The Bob West North field, contained in a total area of over 15,000 acres, was discovered by TransTexas in late 1994. It is located in southern Zapata County, Texas, about three miles north of the older Bob West field.

The new fault block containing the Santos 1 is adjacent to the U.S./Mexican border and opens up an additional productive area in the field that is believed to contain up to 10 additional drilling locations, the company said.
The Santos 1 well extends the Roletta sands 3.3 miles from the original discovery well in the field, the Perez 2.

The company said it has five rigs drilling the development well program in the field, with four additional wells underway, the Vela-Lopeno Minerals Ltd., the Falcon Gas Unit 2, the Palmyra 11 and the M. V. Ramirez 6.
The Vela-Lopeno Minerals is the most northerly well to-date in the existing highly productive fault block of the field, being 2.5 miles north of the Perez 2 discovery well.
The company said it is drilling this well to delineate the northerly extension of the original fault block and establish further drilling locations in that fault block.
